paper2Info.subject: Agriculture, Science & Technology
paper2Info.paperName: Agriculture, Science & Technology Paper 2 (Structured Questions) — Original Practice Bank

sections.A: Structured questions; answer according to the exam configuration.
sections.B: Longer structured/extended questions; answer according to the exam configuration.

paper2Questions.questionText: A farmer notices that the topsoil is being washed away after heavy rain.

subparts.question: State two causes of the problem.
Give two methods of controlling it.

paper2Questions.questionText: A school starts a compost heap using crop residues and kitchen waste.

subparts.question: State two materials that can be composted.
Explain why water is added during compost making.

paper2Questions.questionText: A farmer grows maize and keeps cattle on the same farm.

subparts.question: Name the type of farming enterprise involving both crops and livestock.
Give two benefits of integrating crops and livestock.
Explain how manure can support crop production.

paper2Questions.questionText: A farmer plans to irrigate vegetables during a dry period.

subparts.question: Explain one risk of poor irrigation management.

paper2Questions.questionText: A farmer keeps dairy cattle.

subparts.question: State two requirements for healthy dairy cattle.
Explain why clean water is important.

paper2Questions.questionText: A crop is attacked by insects.

subparts.question: Name two methods of pest control.
Explain why integrated pest management can be useful.

paper2Questions.questionText: A farmer wants to improve soil fertility.

subparts.question: State two benefits of organic manure.
Give one precaution when handling manure.

paper2Questions.questionText: A farmer stores harvested grain for several months.

subparts.question: State one condition required for safe grain storage.
Name two storage pests or problems.
Give two ways of reducing storage losses.

paper2Questions.questionText: A herd of cattle is grazing continuously in one small area.

subparts.question: Name the problem that may result.

paper2Questions.questionText: A farmer wants to reduce livestock disease.
A farmer uses a knapsack sprayer.

subparts.question: State one use of a knapsack sprayer.
Explain why chemical labels must be followed.

paper2Questions.questionText: A farm manager keeps records of sales, inputs and expenses.

subparts.question: State two benefits of farm records.

paper2Questions.questionText: A farmer wants to reduce financial risk.

subparts.question: State two ways of reducing risk.

paper2Questions.questionText: A farmer selects healthy seeds before planting.

subparts.question: State one characteristic of good seed.
Give two reasons for using good seed.
State one condition needed for germination.

paper2Questions.questionText: A farmer uses crop rotation.

subparts.question: Explain how rotation can help manage pests or fertility.

paper2Questions.questionText: A farmer wants to protect a stream beside a field.

subparts.question: Name one source of agricultural water pollution.
State two ways of protecting the stream.
Explain why water conservation is important.

paper2Questions.questionText: A learner investigates why some plants grow faster than others.

subparts.question: Name one factor affecting plant growth.
State two environmental requirements of plants.
Explain the role of light in photosynthesis.

paper2Questions.questionText: A learner observes a leaf under suitable conditions.

subparts.question: Name the process by which green plants make food.
State one product of the process.

paper2Questions.questionText: A learner measures the temperature of water before and after heating.

subparts.question: Explain what happens to particles as water is heated.

paper2Questions.questionText: A simple electric circuit contains a cell, wires, a switch and a lamp.

subparts.question: State the condition needed for the lamp to light.
Explain the function of the switch.

paper2Questions.questionText: A learner compares transparent, translucent and opaque materials.

subparts.question: Give one example of an opaque material.

paper2Questions.questionText: A family wants to reduce electricity use.

subparts.question: State two ways of saving electricity.
Explain one advantage of renewable energy.

paper2Questions.questionText: A learner investigates friction by moving objects over different surfaces.

subparts.question: Explain how surface texture affects friction.

paper2Questions.questionText: A learner studies a food chain in a grassland.

subparts.question: Explain the direction of energy transfer.

paper2Questions.questionText: A pond becomes polluted with waste.

subparts.question: Suggest two ways to reduce the pollution.

paper2Questions.questionText: A learner studies the human digestive system.

subparts.question: Name the organ where digestion begins.
State one function of the stomach.
Explain why the small intestine is important.

paper2Questions.questionText: A learner investigates disease prevention.

subparts.question: State two ways of reducing transmission.

paper2Questions.questionText: A learner observes day and night.

subparts.question: Name the movement responsible for day and night.
State the approximate time Earth takes to complete one rotation.
Explain why different places experience different times of day.

paper2Questions.questionText: A class investigates water changing state.

subparts.question: Name the change from liquid to gas.
Name the change from gas to liquid.
Give one example of each change in everyday life.

paper2Questions.questionText: A learner uses a microscope to observe a specimen.

subparts.question: State the purpose of a microscope.
Give one rule for handling it safely.
Explain why very small structures can be studied with it.

paper2Questions.questionText: A class tests a hypothesis by changing one factor at a time.

subparts.question: Why should other relevant conditions be controlled?
State one way of recording results.

paper2Questions.questionText: A learner finds that an iron nail rusts faster in a wet place.

subparts.question: State two conditions that encourage rusting.
Suggest one method of preventing rust.

paper2Questions.questionText: A learner studies magnets.

subparts.question: Name one material attracted by a magnet.
What happens when like poles are brought together?

paper2Questions.questionText: A family wants to reduce household waste.

subparts.question: Give two materials that can be recycled.

paper2Questions.questionText: A school uses computers for research and presentations.

subparts.question: State one benefit of ICT in learning.

paper2Questions.questionText: A learner creates a password for an online account.

subparts.question: State two characteristics of a strong password.
Give one reason passwords should remain private.
State one action to take if an account is compromised.

paper2Questions.questionText: A class stores learner information in a database.

subparts.question: State two benefits of organising information in a database.

paper2Questions.questionText: A learner prepares a presentation for a science project.

subparts.question: State two features that can make a presentation clear.
Give one rule for responsible use of images or information.

paper2Questions.questionText: Two learners communicate using an internet-based voice call.

subparts.question: Name the technology generally associated with internet voice calls.
Give one safety or privacy precaution.

paper2Questions.questionText: A school computer has been infected by malicious software.

subparts.question: Name the general term for such malicious software.
Name one tool used to help detect it.

subparts.question: Explain how it can reduce soil erosion.

subparts.question: Explain why clean nesting areas are useful.

subparts.question: Give one importance to crop pollination.
